programme: RBPJ (CSL), acting as the DNA-binding core of canonical Notch signaling, driving its own canonical effector set — HES1, HEY1, HEY2, NOTCH1, NOTCH3, DLK1, LFNG — the textbook Notch/RBPJ transcriptional module
role_in_a: In stroke, RBPJ-transduced Notch signaling (via NOTCH3 in vascular mural cells) maintains cerebral small-vessel integrity; the retrieved models show Rbpj loss disrupting vascular remodeling (Apelin/Cdc42), pericyte-endothelial coupling, and driving aberrant CNS macrophage states after ischemic injury.
role_in_b: In the thymus, RBPJ transducing NOTCH1 signaling is the master switch for T-cell lineage commitment and thymocyte maturation in the cortico-medullary niche; dysregulated Notch-RBPJ activity is a recurrent feature of thymic lymphoid/epithelial neoplasia, so a residual role in thymoma is expected even though it is not this tissue's top-ranked association.
shared_axis: Both diseases depend on the same RBPJ-Notch module to set the identity of a non-parenchymal niche cell population — vascular mural/glial cells in cerebral tissue for stroke, epithelial-lymphoid stromal cells in the thymus for thymoma — so the pairing reflects reuse of one transcriptional switch in two different niche contexts rather than a shared cell type or organ.
reasoning: RBPJ's own target signature is unambiguously canonical Notch, and three retrieved papers independently place Rbpj-dependent signaling in stroke-relevant cerebrovascular pathology, satisfying placement in at least one disease. But no retrieved paper places RBPJ in thymoma specifically, and Open Targets ranks it low there (10th percentile vs. 90th in stroke), so the thymoma side of the connection rests on general Notch/thymocyte biology rather than on the evidence supplied.
support: PMID 39890825 - Rbpj-deficient CNS macrophages show region-specific immunogenic states, a stroke-relevant neuroinflammatory phenotype. PMID 37051908 - Rbpj deficiency disrupts vascular remodeling via Apelin/Cdc42, a direct mechanistic link to cerebrovascular integrity. PMID 36147294 - Rbpj loss causes pathological pericyte expansion and impaired pericyte-endothelial communication, a stroke-relevant vascular defect.
how_to_falsify: Check whether RBPJ occupies and regulates its canonical targets (HES1, HEY1, NOTCH3) in thymoma tissue versus normal thymus, and whether conditional Rbpj deletion in thymic epithelium or T-lineage progenitors produces a thymoma-relevant phenotype; if RBPJ binding/activity at these targets is absent or unchanged in thymoma, the thymoma arm of the claim fails. If Notch pathway inhibition fails to worsen vascular remodeling in the Rbpj-sufficient stroke models cited, the stroke arm fails.
caveats: Blood/thymus is a vascular-versus-epithelial-lymphoid pairing, so 'shared axis' means a shared pathway logic, not a shared cell type. Only 30 patient-group comparisons across 2 independent cohort pairs back this result, and RBPJ's 27/30 concordance, while strong, is not the highest in the set (RERE reaches 29/30 but has no literature support at all). The tissue-generic filter already removed CIITA, TBX21, SPIB, BCL6, ETS2 — classic thymic/immune master regulators — which is why RBPJ's survival is notable rather than a generic thymic signal. The other 11 concordant factors (RERE, GFI1B, ZBTB18, AKNA, ZNF277, FOXS1, ISL1, PITX1, HMX1, NR2E1, NCOA4) do not integrate into this Notch module; ISL1 and NCOA4 in particular have independent, unrelated literature support (endocrine/cardiac-progenitor biology and ferritinophagy/ferroptosis respectively) that could motivate a separate account for this pair but is not combined here.
